question: Should OpenClaw adopt the new public PluginManifest.safetyEventTypes and OpenClawPluginServiceContext.safetyDiagnostics.emit contract as a supported plugin API, or keep this initial taxonomy core-owned until a narrower SDK design is approved?
rationale: The patch creates a new plugin manifest permission and public service-context capability whose long-term compatibility, authorization semantics, and operator-data contract cannot be selected safely by an automated review.

options.title: Approve a narrow plugin API
options.body: Sponsor the capability with a documented event/payload/privacy contract, compatibility tests, and explicit external-plugin authorization semantics before merge.

options.title: Keep v1 core-owned
options.body: Remove the public manifest and service-context API from this PR, retain only core emitters and internal exporter integration, and propose a separately reviewed plugin SDK surface later.

options.title: Pause the feature bundle
options.body: Close or split the PR until the diagnostics, storage-retention, and plugin ownership design has an approved maintainer direction.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow plugin API
recommendation.body: Sponsor the capability with a documented event/payload/privacy contract, compatibility tests, and explicit external-plugin authorization semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The necessary decision spans the plugin SDK, diagnostics, persistent operator data, and security-trust boundaries; current-main ownership could not be established from the available read-only evidence.
